content: 1. The effectiveness of oral ampicillin may be reduced when co-administered with agents that increase gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Clarithromycin can increase the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting the metabolism of CYP3A4 enzymes in the liver and intestines. Caution and monitoring are recommended. When apalutamide is co-administered with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors, initial dosage adjustments are not required, but dose reductions may be necessary based on patient tolerability. 3. Both arformoterol and clarithromycin can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Armodafinil increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism in the liver. Similarly, clarithromycin increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The recommended atogepant dose is 10 mg orally once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 8. Omeprazole increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Both azithromycin and clarithromycin can prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin can also increase the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Both clarithromycin and bedaquiline can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring, including ECG monitoring, are required. 13. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of belumosudil by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The belumosudil dose should be increased to 200 mg orally twice daily when co-administered with proton pump inhibitors. 14. Omeprazole increases the levels or effects of belzutifan by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Belzutifan is a CYP2C19 substrate, and co-administration with CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase the risk or severity of adverse effects. 15. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. If co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate as per its prescribing information. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. 17. Bortezomib increases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat and betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. For betrixaban, the dose should be reduced to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally once daily when co-administered with a P-gp inhibitor. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 21. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of bortezomib and bosentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 22. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of bosutinib by approximately 45% due to its pH-dependent solubility. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring for adverse reactions are advised. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. The brexpiprazole dose should be halved when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor is also administered, the dose should be reduced to a quarter. 25. Clarithromycin increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole decreases budesonide effects by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be reduced or discontinued, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 28. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of omeprazole by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injections by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. If signs of buprenorphine toxicity occur, transition the patient back to a formulation that allows dose adjustments. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, requiring dose adjustments of calcifediol. 31. Cannabidiol increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cannabidiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 32. Omeprazole decreases the effects of capecitabine, likely due to impaired dissolution and absorption caused by elevated gastric pH. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Carbamazepine decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Omeprazole decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 37. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefpodoxime, and cefuroxime due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 38. Omeprazole decreases the effects of cefpodoxime and cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Cenobamate increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Clarithromycin increases ceritinib levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Omeprazole decreases ciprofloxacin levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Clarithromycin increases cholic acid toxicity by reducing its elimination. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 45. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Cimetidine increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Omeprazole increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. The maximum recommended citalopram dose is 20 mg/day due to the risk of QT prolongation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Clarithromycin increases clevidipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Omeprazole increases clobazam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 50. Clarithromycin increases clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Clarithromycin increases clorazepate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Cobicistat increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Conivaptan increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Clarithromycin decreases conjugated estrogen levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone, with a low risk of contraceptive failure. Clarithromycin also increases conjugated estrogen levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Omeprazole decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces its solubility and bioavailability. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Clarithromycin increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Crofelemer increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the gut. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 58. Omeprazole and cyclosporine may increase each other's toxicity. Long-term PPI use may cause hypomagnesemia, increasing the risk of cyclosporine toxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Clarithromycin increases cyclosporine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Clarithromycin increases dabigatran levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Avoid co-administration in patients with reduced renal function (CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment). 61. Dabrafenib decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 62. Clarithromycin increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 63. Omeprazole reduces the time to Tmax for dextroamphetamine due to reduced gastric acidity, but AUC remains unaffected. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 64. Clarithromycin increases darolutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 65. Clarithromycin increases darunavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 66. Clarithromycin and dasatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 67. Clarithromycin increases daunorubicin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 68. Deferasirox decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 69. Clarithromycin increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 70. Clarithromycin and deutetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 71. Clarithromycin increases dexamethasone levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 72. Clarithromycin increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Omeprazole also increases diazepam levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 73. Dichlorphenamide and omeprazole both decrease serum potassium levels. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 74. Clarithromycin increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. It also decreases their levels by altering intestinal flora. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 75. Clarithromycin increases digoxin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Omeprazole increases digoxin toxicity due to hypomagnesemia caused by prolonged PPI use. Caution and monitoring are advised. 76. Clarithromycin increases diltiazem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 77. Efavirenz increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases omeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 78. Clarithromycin increases disopyramide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 79. Clarithromycin increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 80. Clarithromycin and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 81. Clarithromycin increases donepezil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 82. Clarithromycin increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 83. Clarithromycin increases doxepin cream levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 84. Clarithromycin increases doxorubicin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 85. Clarithromycin increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 86. Clarithromycin increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 87. Clarithromycin increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 88. Clarithromycin increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 89. Elagolix increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 90. Clarithromycin increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 91. Omeprazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended.
